title: US markets closed — Independence Day observed on Monday, July 5 (equities and USD fixed income both dark; the only 2027 full market closure this calendar does not track)
source: NEWS: two primaries, both fetched and parsed first-hand on 2026-09-08 by the sifma-bond-market-closure-2027-11-11 initial research. (1) nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes): all 109 data cells were extracted, and the 2027 column of the Independence Day row reads verbatim 'Monday, July 5 (Independence Day observed) ' — NYSE's own grid, whose header states its ten holidays apply to all NYSE markets for 2026, 2027 and 2028. The observance follows mechanically from 5 U.S.C. 6103, which moves a Sunday federal holiday to the following Monday, and 2027-07-04 is a Sunday. (2) sifma.org/resources/general/holiday-schedule (HTTP 200, 299,159 bytes): the 2027 US panel's card 75, decoded from the page's RSC payload, reads 'U.S. Independence Day' / 'Monday, July 5, 2027' / 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Friday, July 2, 2027' — so the recommended USD fixed-income tape is dark on the Monday too, not merely shortened. Filed estimate on two counts, neither of which is doubt about the date: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange's or a trade association's own holiday calendar (the same gap labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07, good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26 and memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31 each recorded), and a discovering lane may not self-confirm an event it found in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: HONEST SCOPE NOTE, STATED FIRST: 2027-07-05 is D-129 from the proposing event and therefore far OUTSIDE its +/-5-day corridor, and its id class ('*-market-closure' for a full cross-asset holiday) is not the proposer's own. It is proposed anyway because it is the largest gap the proposing session's calendar diff turned up and it was read first-hand off the same two fetches the proposer's own source rests on. Nothing in the proposing event's stance depends on it. WHY IT IS A HOLE: the proposing session diffed all sixteen 2027 US SIFMA holiday/early-close dates against every tracked file and proposal. Fourteen are tracked — mlk-market-closure-2027-01-18, presidents-day-market-closure-2027-02-15, good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26, memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31, juneteenth-market-closure-2027-06-18, labor-day-market-closure-2027-09-06, sifma-bond-holiday-close-2027-10-11, thanksgiving-market-closure-2027-11-25, christmas-market-closure-2027-12-24 and the early closes around them — and exactly two are not: this one and the 2027-07-02 bond early close paired with it (proposed as sifma-bond-early-close-2027-07-02.from-sifma-bond-market-closure-2027-11-11.json). Every other 2027 full US market closure has an entry, which makes this an omission rather than a policy. It is also the only 2027 closure that is an OBSERVED shift rather than a holiday landing on a weekday, which is the likeliest reason a date-driven sweep missed it. HONEST LIMITS. (1) Filed 'sector' to match the id class of the other full cross-asset closures on this calendar rather than the proposer's 'rates'; EventKind has no market-structure member either way. (2) Whether NYSE also runs a shortened Friday 2027-07-02 equity session is NOT asserted — the NYSE grid names only the Monday holiday, and the SIFMA card's 2:00 p.m. note is about fixed income. (3) Nasdaq, CME and Treasury settlement behaviour on 2027-07-05 are not asserted; only the two sources above were read. (4) Anyone taking this entry should check whether it duplicates a differently-named tracked event before writing the canonical file — the proposing session searched by DATE across all canonical files and proposals and found none, which is the strongest check available but not a name-space proof. Impact low, symbols [] — a closure moves nothing by itself; estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
